text: A decade of launches from the edge of the world 🚀 🇳🇿 Ten years ago, Launch Complex 1 was officially opened and became the world's first private orbital launch site. What seemed like a crazy idea - making dedicated launches to space frequent and affordable from a farm paddock in New Zealand - is now routine. Across Electron's history, LC-1 has been the launch location for commercial smallsats and science missions, national security payloads, and even a mission to the Moon. Two launch pads and almost 100 launches later, LC-1 has made New Zealand one of the world's busiest launch countries - proving big things can happen in the most unexpected locations.

Electron launches for the 97th time and deploys the latest StriX satellite to space for synspective from Launch Complex 1. Highlights from today's mission: ✅ Launched on 1st attempt ✅ 18th mission of the year ✅ 13th launch for Synspective with 100% mission success
